findings.rule: When an exit branch of a 'while True' body never continues the loop (it returns, breaks or reverts), emit it after the loop: 'while not c: body' followed by that branch's code; reached-by-break tails merge after the loop only when they are the same code.

findings.rule: As c00600's shape A: 'while t < n: mem[d + t] = mem[a + t]; t += 32' followed by 'mem[d + n] = 0' is 'mem[d len n] = mem[a len n]' plus padding; a store fully overwritten before any read is dead.

notes: Decoder-and-sanitizer contract: 166 small functions that check calldata and return abi.encodePacked(addresses...). Reviewed all functions with loops in detail and sampled the straight-line ones (approve, deposit*, withdraw*, borrow/repay/supply variants, bridge*, operate*, swapCompact): they decode calldata, apply the source's reverts (custom errors such as 0x82cc44c9 NoBytes) and return 'Array(len=40, data=Bytes(20, _param1), Bytes(20, _param2))'-style packed bytes, matching the source. Source loops: 23, all whiles: ccipSend (2958), claim (1631), both completeQueuedWithdrawals with their nested fors (2187/2220/2244, 2299/2332/2356), exactInput's hop loop (1772, bound printed as 'cd[..] / 23'), exitPool (1473), joinPool (1523), fill (1688), flashLoan (1423), lockOffers (1563), queueWithdrawals' nested fors (1833/1840), redeemDueInterestAndRewards' 3 fors (1907, 1926, 1945), send's 'while (cursor < opts.length)' (3108), uniswapV3Swap (1044), _sanitizeLimitOrderData's 2 fors (nested in the text, finding 1). The 62 other whiles are implicit: 55 memory-to-memory copies (P7, finding 2), calldata decodes with validation, and ccipSend's copy of a calldata struct array 'while idx < ..: mem[s] = cd[idx]' (could be a copy line).
